title: New NORDIS report highlights lessons from Nordic media literacy initiatives
content:
A new NORDIS report reviews 14 media literacy events and campaigns across the Nordic countries, highlighting lessons learned and a growing focus on artificial intelligence. The partners now aim to build on these experiences by equipping teachers and librarians with tools to help young people navigate an increasingly AI-driven information landscape.

The new NORDIS report Literacy events and campaigns documents what the NORDIS partners Faktabaari, Faktisk.no (Tenk), TjekDet and Källkritikbyrån delivered between May 2024 and October 2026.

They are in short:

  • 3 events and 11 campaigns in Finnish, Norwegian, Danish, Swedish and English.
  • AI and recommendation algorithms as the common challenge to digital infomation literacy, from the Faktabaari AI Guide for Teachers (launched at the NORDIS Digital Information Literacy Forum in Helsinki, January 2025) to Tenk’s AI teaching package and search course in Norway and TjekDet’s “Hey Chat… Who Should I Vote For?”material ahead of the Danish election in March 2026.

title: Finding the claims worth checking: How AI-assisted monitoring can support fact-checking journalism
content:
One of the major challenges facing fact-checking newsrooms is identifying the claims that deserve investigation in the first place. With misleading statements scattered across social media, podcasts, television and radio, journalists cannot possibly monitor everything. NORDIS has during the last two years been testing how AI-assisted monitoring can help address this challenge.

For fact-checkers, verifying a claim is only part of the job. Before journalists can investigate whether a statement is true, misleading or false, they first need to discover it.

This has become increasingly difficult as public debate takes place across a growing number of digital platforms, some of which are difficult to monitor systematically. Even traditional, lengthy political debates in parliaments and discussions on television and radio programmes generate hours of content containing potentially checkable statements.

NORDIS has for the last couple of years been testing and using technology developed by Norwegian company Factiverse to explore how automated monitoring can support editorial research and help journalists identify claims they might otherwise miss.
